rationale: ram_zeroshot-claude-agentic: ram_ckpt_path=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/ram.pth.tar, ram_input_norm=adjoint_max, ram_clamp_output=True, ram_finetune=False, ram_finetune_epochs=0, ram_finetune_lr=0.0001, ram_disable_multiscale=True, ram_disable_cudnn=False, ram_use_deepinv_tomo=False, ram_sigma=0.02, ram_factor=0.55, ram_post_fbp_blend=0.3, val_n=214, rationale=iter-4 (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol) CONFIRMATION iter. ONE knob = the LAST untried RAM hyperparameter: ram_sigma 0.005->0.02 (4x). All other knobs RETURN to the iter-1 point (ram_factor 0.2->0.55, ram_post_fbp_blend 0.3, adjoint_max norm, multiscale disabled, finetune OFF) so the ONLY change vs iter-1 is the denoiser noise-conditioning, isolating ram_sigma cleanly. cfg_full audit: across iters 1-3 ram_sigma sat at its CONFIG DEFAULT 5e-3 and was NEVER moved, whereas ram_input_norm was already set off-default to adjoint_max at iter-1 -> ram_sigma is the one remaining knob still at default. SEMANTICS (solver_ram.py L15/L327/L346): ram_sigma is the Gaussian noise-level conditioning passed to physics.noise_model (dinv.physics.GaussianNoise(sigma=ram_sigma)) -- it tells the pretrained RAM denoiser HOW NOISY to treat the input, i.e. the prior STRENGTH, which is the core mechanism by which RAM is supposed to add recoverable signal beyond its FBP init. Raising it 4x (0.005->0.02) makes RAM denoise MORE aggressively -- the most aggressive single-knob test of whether the RAM prior carries ANY LDCT-specific recoverable signal at ANY strength. Trajectory under the corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric: iter-1 SSIM 0.8611 hr 0.0 (blend0.3/factor0.55/sigma0.005); iter-2 SSIM 0.8644 hr EXACTLY 0.0 (blend0.3->0.5 -- post-hoc linear FBP/RAM mix EXHAUSTED); iter-3 SSIM 0.8968 hr 0.0 (factor0.55->0.2 -- internal prox_l2 DC gain EXHAUSTED; weakening the DC realign RAISED raw SSIM +0.033 but kept calibrated headroom pinned at 0.0). SSIM rose 0.861->0.864->0.897 yet PSNR stayed below the LD-FBP floor on the RMSE-sensitive calibrated metric throughout (baseline LD-FBP 0.8078, oracle HD-FBP 0.9331). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS, not CT pixels): (1) prev result: hr 0.0 on all of post-hoc blend AND internal prox_l2 gain; (2) FBP-bound named: RAM is a pretrained zero-shot deepinv recon that never saw real LDCT helical-rebinned 2304-view fan data; its denoiser prior adds no recoverable signal over FBP on dense Mayo -> the calibrated headroom is pinned at the LD-FBP floor (hr=0) regardless of which inference knob moves; (3) ONE knob: ram_sigma 0.005->0.02 (the last untried hyperparameter, the denoiser prior strength); (4) hypothesis: hr stays EXACTLY 0.0 -- the noise-conditioning does not matter because the RAM prior carries no LDCT-specific signal; predict hr 0; (5) falsifier: if hr at ram_sigma=0.02 != 0.0 (rises OR drops), RAM's denoiser strength DOES move the metric and RAM is NOT purely FBP-bounded; (6) verdict trigger: if hr stays 0.0 across the post-hoc blend (iter-2), the internal prox_l2 gain (iter-3), AND now the denoiser noise-conditioning (iter-4), RAM is CONFIRMED structurally FBP-bounded on dense Mayo across ALL three inference levers -> FILE FBP-BOUND NEGATIVE RESULT, STOP iterating this solver. Budget: only a scalar GaussianNoise sigma changes -> zero added compute vs iter-3 (iter-2 ran 1100.9 s = 18.3 min for 214 single forward passes + one op-norm power iter), inside the HARD 20-min train+score budget; sbatch --time=00:30:00 backstop wall. val_n stays 214 (score ALL L277 slices @ 321px detector-geometry FOV). HARD-WIRED: staged_canonical, v3 mayo_ldct_fitted, per-sample-ps, bg_target=truth, 321px FOV default.
